children: Coal India Ltd. (NSE:COALINDIA) boosted thermal dispatch and e-auction volumes in October even as coal stocks fell and 79 plants remain critical, supporting higher realizations and a raised FY26 payout (Rs5.25 final; Rs26.40 total) amid large cash reserves and lower leverage in the stock.
Coal India Ltd. Stock Piles Decline
: Coal India (COALINDIA): domestic coal stocks at 176 coal-fired power plants were 18.22–18.25 MT in early October, down ~3.8% week-over-week; 79 plants in critical stock position.
Coal India Dispatch Up; October Higher
: Coal India (COALINDIA) raised thermal dispatch: ~1.81 mt/day Oct 1–3 and ~1.78 mt/day so far in October vs 1.63 mt/day in September; October dispatch ~9% higher. Daily demand ~2.95 mt/day.
: Coal India (COALINDIA): e-auction volumes rising, stronger realizations in north; near-term price band seen ~₹420–425 to ₹450–460; dividend yield ~6% noted for traders.
: Coal India (COALINDIA) declared a FY26 final dividend of Rs5.25/share (record date Sept 4, 2026). Total FY26 payout Rs26.40/share vs Rs25.50 in FY25; interim payouts were Rs5.50 each.
Coal India H1 FY27 Pithead Sale
: In H1 FY27 Coal India Ltd. sold 63 million tonnes of pithead coal, noting this inventory drawdown supported higher supply during that period.
Coal India Holds Large Cash Reserves
: Coal India Ltd. (COALINDIA) holds large cash reserves; a 25 bp RBI rate hike could boost treasury income and returns from redeploying funds into higher-yielding instruments.
: Coal India (COALINDIA) saw margin trading exposure drop 31% in September, signaling a notable cut in leveraged positions held in the stock compared with the prior period.
